transcript.text: I cannot provide specific advice without knowing the make and model of your washing machine. Please check for any error codes on the display or consult the user manual for troubleshooting steps related to a spin failure. From what you have described, the most likely cause is unbalanced / uneven load. Is the drum empty of water when it tries to spin, or is there water still in it?
drum is empty of water, no water left. its a hotpoint, just the one wet bath mat came out dripping

This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: Machines deliberately skip or reduce the spin when a load is unbalanced (one heavy item, a small load, a duvet or a bath mat). Clothes then come out wet. It would be worth a closer look if it never spins even with a normal mixed load, or it hums without draining. Washing machines refuse to spin if the load is out of balance — a single heavy item such as a bath mat, rug, duvet or a pair of jeans on its own, or a very small load, is the usual trigger. Spreading the washing out evenly or adding a few smaller items usually lets it spin. Was it a single heavy item or a very small load, or a normal mixed load?
just the one heavy rubber backed bath mat on its own, nothing else in with it. so is that why it wont spin?

Yes, an unbalanced load like a single rubber-backed bath mat can prevent the washing machine from spinning to protect the drum. The machine detects this imbalance and stops the cycle for safety reasons. Does it keep turning slowly backwards and forwards as if trying to balance the load, and does it spin fine with a different, evenly-spread load?
yeah it sloshes back n forth, tries to speed up then slows down a few times. a full load yesterday spun fine tho. so what do i do with the mat?

Remove the wet bath mat from the drum immediately. Dry it thoroughly before washing again, as heavy items like this can unbalance the machine and prevent spinning. If you haven't already, change that (switch the option off, or even out the load), then run a rinse and spin or spin-only programme to test it. Does it spin up properly now?
havent tried it yet. do i just put the mat back in on its own and run rinse n spin? its still dripping

Yes, you can try running a Rinse & Spin cycle with just the single heavy item to see if it balances correctly. If the machine still struggles or stops, the issue may be related to an unbalanced load rather than a mechanical fault. Next: Try a normal, evenly-distributed load before suspecting a part. Let me know what you find.
